steps.description:
Write a function that takes in a string in the format "a/b" representing a fraction (where a is the numerator and b is the denominator). It will display the numerator and denominator on separate rows.

Write a program to ask user to input a string in the format "a/b" representing a fraction. It will then call your function to perform the action.

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.

Test Input 4/12

7/4

16/4

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Input a fraction (a/b): 4/12 4 12

Example 2 Input a fraction (a/b): 7/4 7 4

Example 3 Input a fraction (a/b): 16/4 16 4

Write a function that takes in a string in the format "a/b" representing a fraction (where a is the numerator and b is the denominator). If it is an improper fraction (i.e. numerator is equal to or bigger than the denominator), the function will compute and return the whole number. For example, if "13/6" is the input string, "2" will be returned. Otherwise, 0 will be returned.

Write a program to ask user to input a string in the format "a/b" representing a fraction. It will then call your function to compute the whole number and display the returned result.

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.

Hint: - The floor division operator // returns the quotient of a division. Eg. 7//3 gives you 2

Test Input 4/12

7/4

16/4

29/9

0/9

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Input a fraction (a/b): 4/12 0

Example 2 Input a fraction (a/b): 7/4 1

Example 3 Input a fraction (a/b): 16/4 4

Example 4 Input a fraction (a/b): 29/9 3

Example 5 Input a fraction (a/b): 0/9 0

Write a function that takes in a string in the format "a/b" representing a fraction (where a is the numerator and b is the denominator). It will compute and return the whole number and the proper fraction as a string if they are not zero. However, if both whole number and numerator are zeros, return "0".

For example, 13/6 will give 2 1/6, so return "2 1/6" 4/4 will give 1 0/4, so return "1" 3/7 will give 0 3/7, so return "3/7" 0/3 will give 0 0/3, so return "0"

Write a program to ask user to input a string in the format "a/b" representing a fraction. It will then call your function and display the returned result.

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.

Test Input 4/12

7/4

16/4

33/9

0/9

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Test your program with the 5 examples below: Input a fraction (a/b): 4/12 4/12

Input a fraction (a/b): 7/4 1 3/4

Input a fraction (a/b): 16/4 4

Input a fraction (a/b): 33/9 3 6/9

Input a fraction (a/b): 0/9 0

Write a function that takes a string in the format "a/b" representing a fraction (where a is the numerator and b is the denominator). It will compute its simple fraction and return the result as a string. Zero whole number or fraction with zero numerator will be excluded. However, if both whole number and numerator are zeros, return "0".

For example, "4/12" returns "1/3", "7/4" returns "1 3/4". For example, 4/12 will give 0 1/3, so return "1/3" 6/4 will give 1 1/2, so return "1 1/2" 28/7 will give 4 0/7, so return "4" 0/3 will give 0 0/3, so return "0"

Write a program to ask user to input a string in the format "a/b" representing a fraction. It will then call your function to compute the simple fraction and display the returned result.

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.

Hint: - Try to simplify by dividing bigger number first.
